# Disagreement Log — Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 67

**Date:** 2026-03-17
**Agents:** EMET (literal) | LOGOS (formal) | PNEUMA (dynamic)
**Total Disagreements:** 9

---

## Disagreement 1 — 67:1 "how long will you be without understanding" vs. "how long will you persist in your lack of understanding"

- **EMET:** "how long will you be without understanding"
- **LOGOS:** "how long will you persist in your lack of understanding"
- **PNEUMA:** "how long are you going to be slow to understand things"
- **Greek:** *poson chronon asynetos esei* — how long will you be without understanding
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "how long will you persist in your lack of understanding" (LOGOS). "Persist" adds the iterative aspect — the Shepherd has explained things many times; PNEUMA's "slow to understand" is less precise.

---

## Disagreement 2 — 67:1 "you are too persistent" vs. "too persistent in your questioning"

- **EMET:** "you are too persistent"
- **LOGOS:** "you are too persistent in your questioning"
- **PNEUMA:** "You're too persistent"
- **Note:** EMET and PNEUMA agree; LOGOS specifies "in your questioning."
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "you are too persistent in your questioning" (LOGOS). The context makes clear that the persistence is in questioning; adding "in your questioning" makes this explicit.

---

## Disagreement 3 — 67:2 "sin each day" vs. "sin every single day"

- **EMET:** "they sin each day, though with small sins"
- **LOGOS:** "they sin each day, though their sins are small"
- **PNEUMA:** "They sin every single day — but the sins are small ones"
- **Greek:** *kath' hēmeran hamartanousin oligan* — they sin daily in small ways
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "they sin each day, though their sins are small" (LOGOS). "Each day" preserves the temporal regularity; "every single day" (PNEUMA) over-emphasizes.

---

## Disagreement 4 — 67:2 "in word, in deed, even in thought" — all agree

- **EMET:** "in speech and in action and even in thought"
- **LOGOS:** "in word, in deed, even in thought"
- **PNEUMA:** "in what they say, in what they do, even in what they think"
- **Note:** All three agree on the triadic structure.
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "in word, in deed, even in thought" (LOGOS). The concise traditional triplet is most elegant.

---

## Disagreement 5 — 67:2 "lighter afflictions" vs. "lesser ways" vs. "light afflictions"

- **EMET:** "torments them in lesser ways"
- **LOGOS:** "torments them with lighter afflictions"
- **PNEUMA:** "He gives them only light afflictions"
- **Greek:** *en olígois basanisthēsontai* — they will be tormented in few/lesser ways
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "torments them with lighter afflictions" (LOGOS). "Lighter" conveys the comparative degree well; "lesser ways" (EMET) is grammatically awkward.

---

## Disagreement 6 — 67:3 "great and accumulated sins" vs. "great sins piled one on another"

- **EMET:** "those who have great and accumulated sins"
- **LOGOS:** "those who have great and accumulated sins"
- **PNEUMA:** "those who have committed great sins, piled one on another"
- **Note:** EMET and LOGOS agree.
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "those who have great and accumulated sins" (EMET/LOGOS). "Accumulated" captures the progressive building-up of sin.

---

## Disagreement 7 — 67:3 "salvation is delayed" vs. "long delayed" vs. "take a long time"

- **EMET:** "their salvation is delayed"
- **LOGOS:** "their salvation will be long delayed"
- **PNEUMA:** "it's going to take a long time"
- **Greek:** *bradyterou sōthēsontai* — they will be saved more slowly
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "their salvation will be long delayed" (LOGOS). The comparative *bradyterou* = more slowly/more tardily; "long delayed" captures this well.

---

## Disagreement 8 — 67:5 "losses and wanderings" — treatment

- **EMET:** "losses, and wanderings, and various illnesses"
- **LOGOS:** "losses, and wanderings, and various illnesses"
- **PNEUMA:** "losses of all kinds, aimless wandering, various illnesses"
- **Note:** EMET and LOGOS agree; PNEUMA adds "aimless" and "all kinds."
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "losses, and wanderings, and various illnesses." The list is preserved as stated; PNEUMA adds interpretive glosses.

---

## Disagreement 9 — 67:5 "the Lord, who is rich in mercy, chastises them"

- **EMET:** "the Lord, who is rich in mercy, chastises them"
- **LOGOS:** "the Lord, who is rich in mercy, chastises them"
- **PNEUMA:** "The Lord, who is abundantly merciful, uses these to discipline them"
- **Note:** EMET and LOGOS agree exactly.
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "the Lord, who is rich in mercy, chastises them" (EMET/LOGOS). *Plousios en elei* = "rich in mercy" (cf. Eph 2:4); this is a recognized divine title worth preserving verbatim.

---

*End of disagreement log for Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 67.*
